title: memQ and Infleqtion Sign MoU to Validate Quantum Networking Interoperability for Distributed Neutral-Atom Systems - Quantum Computing Report
author: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
text:
Quantum networking company memQ and neutral-atom quantum technology provider Infleqtion (NYSE: INFQ) have signed a memorandum of understanding (MoU) to pursue interoperability validation and certification between memQ’s extensible quantum network architecture (xQNA) and Infleqtion’s Sqale quantum computing platform and Superstaq software stack. The collaboration targets modular multi-processor scaling by enabling separate quantum processing units to connect and distribute workloads without collapsing quantum states.

Because conventional data-center interconnects cannot preserve entanglement across independent quantum nodes, optical quantum networking is required to replicate the horizontal clustering model used in classical high-performance computing (HPC). Under the agreement, the two companies will evaluate how memQ’s optical connectivity and quantum control hardware interface with Infleqtion’s neutral-atom architecture and compiler workflows to support flexible, multi-system deployment configurations.

The announcement follows Infleqtion’s 100-qubit Sqale deployment at the U.K. National Quantum Computing Centre and its roadmap to scale toward 1,000 logical qubits by 2030. While the MoU represents an early-stage validation framework subject to technical integration milestones, both companies noted that standardized QPU-to-QPU networking will be critical for enterprise and HPC data-center adoption.
